questions.q: Why is 'SELECT 1 + 1;' a syntax error on Oracle?
options: Oracle's grammar requires every SELECT statement to include a FROM clause
Oracle doesn't support arithmetic expressions in SELECT
Oracle requires a semicolon before SELECT
1 + 1 is reserved syntax in Oracle for something else
questions.explain: Oracle's SQL grammar mandates a FROM clause on every SELECT, unlike SQL Server, MySQL, and PostgreSQL.

options: A real, built-in Oracle system table with exactly one row and one column
A reserved keyword with no actual table behind it
A virtual table that only exists in Oracle's documentation, not in real databases
A function that generates random test data
questions.explain: DUAL is a genuine one-row, one-column system table Oracle ships specifically so SELECT statements can satisfy the mandatory FROM clause when no real table is needed.

questions.q: Do SQL Server, MySQL, and PostgreSQL require a FROM clause for a query like 'SELECT 1+1'?
options: No — all three allow a SELECT with no FROM clause at all
Yes, all three require it just like Oracle
Only SQL Server requires it
Only PostgreSQL requires it
questions.explain: SQL Server, MySQL, and PostgreSQL all allow a bare SELECT <expression> with no FROM clause whatsoever.

questions.q: Why does MySQL support 'SELECT 1+1 FROM DUAL' even though it doesn't need a FROM clause?
options: As an Oracle-compatibility courtesy for developers and migration scripts coming from Oracle
Because MySQL secretly does require FROM, contradicting its normal syntax
Because DUAL is a required system table in MySQL too
It's a typo in MySQL's grammar that was never fixed
questions.explain: MySQL accepts FROM DUAL purely as a compatibility nod to Oracle-style code, even though its own grammar never required a FROM clause.

questions.q: What is the correct Oracle idiom to evaluate UPPER('hello') as a one-off expression?
options: SELECT UPPER('hello') FROM DUAL;
SELECT UPPER('hello');
EVALUATE UPPER('hello');
SELECT UPPER('hello') FROM SYS;
questions.explain: Because Oracle requires a FROM clause, the DUAL table is the standard way to evaluate a one-off expression with no real table involved.
